Signals combined into the risk score: document validation, document integrity check, photo authenticity, watchlist lookup, face match, identity cross-check, and live photo verification.
Weights and thresholds are configured and enforced server-side by the scoring engine only — this app cannot read or set them, and no UI path here can ever submit a manually chosen score.

Dashboard for today\'s picture, Verify to check a document, Review for what waits on you or the admin, History for everything you verified, and More for analytics, your profile and settings.

Tap here when a traveller presents a document. The phone finds the photo, MRZ, QR and stamps, reads the text, takes a live photo, and the server checks everything. You then clear it or send it to the admin.
Counted from your real verifications: documents checked today, those waiting for your decision, those with the admin, and the admin\'s responses. Tap a tile to open the list.
How your verifications split into high, medium and low risk. The risk indicator only explains which checks need attention — it is never a verdict about the traveller.
Verifications per day, split into verified, needs attention and not verified. Tap a day for its numbers; switch between 7 and 30 days.
Checked every few seconds: Online (fast), Weak (slow server) or Offline. Offline captures are saved encrypted and sent automatically later.
The admin\'s responses to cases you sent, and your results grouped by high, medium and low risk. A badge shows new responses.

1. Capture the document (camera or gallery).
2. Check the regions and text read on the phone.
3. Take a live photo of the traveller (or skip).
4. The server checks MRZ, QR, stamps, tampering, registry and face.
5. Read the result — every problem is marked on the document — then Clear it or Send it to the admin with the reason written for you.
Hold the whole document inside the green frame — flat, well lit, no glare. The frame shape matches ID cards and passport pages.
Capture takes the photo with the back camera. Gallery picks an existing photo. For this practice we use a synthetic sample passport.
The on-phone detector boxes the photo, MRZ, QR codes and stamps. Only these regions (and the text read here) are sent — never the whole photo.
The phone reads the printed text and the MRZ before anything is sent, and checks the MRZ check digits itself. The server reads the regions again and uses the phone\'s reading only to fill gaps.
The crossing starts from your post (for example Raxaul — India–Nepal). Change it here if the traveller is crossing elsewhere; treaty rules then apply correctly.
Retake if the photo is blurred or cut off; otherwise continue to the live photo.
Take a photo of the person presenting the document. Flip between front and back camera, or skip the face check. Only the face region is sent and compared with the document photo.
The headline, a plain explanation, the checkpoint and border, and a risk indicator. The risk indicator explains which checks need attention — it is never a verdict.
You decide. Clear it, or Send to admin — the reason is written for you from the findings and you can edit it. Sending also attaches the document image and live photo for the admin.
Every finding is boxed in red on the document, so you can check the exact place yourself.
Every field that was read, with where it came from: read by the server, the MRZ, a QR code, or read on the phone.
The document photo next to the live photo, with the similarity. A clear match passes; a borderline score says compare in person; a missing face is never called a mismatch.
Links to earlier screenings: the same face under another name, or the same document number on another case. Here nothing is linked.
Each finding with its reason — here the printed expiry date differs from the MRZ. Tap one to see it on the document; passed checks are listed below.
That is a whole verification. Nothing from this practice was sent or saved. Tap Verify document on the dashboard to check a real document.
Next, let\'s walk through a full screening using sample data — nothing you do in practice mode is saved.
OCR found this field on the document image. That\'s all "Detected" means — nothing has confirmed it yet.
The backend\'s validation engine ran a real checksum here and confirmed it. That\'s the difference from "Detected."
This ties to the traveler\'s actual document number — a confirmed hit against the registry.
This is only a name similarity, not a document-number match. Always apply officer judgment — never treat it the same as an EXACT hit.
